title: Driver is injured when Savoy grass truck crashes
text:
Local News   January 26, 2005
Driver is injured when Savoy grass truck crashes

By Mary Jane Farmer
Herald Democrat

While going to a grass fire Wednesday afternoon, a Savoy grass truck crashed and it's driver was taken to a local hospital after being thrown through the window.

It happened about 4 p.m. on FM 1752, about a mile south of Savoy. Officials at the scene, including Savoy Mayor Clete Stogsdill and Assistant Fire Chief Michael Halford, said Travis Burks was driving the truck when it left the roadway on the left side, then crossed back over to the right.

His father is Savoy Fire Chief Billy Burks, who said he understands that the truck rolled at least three times. It ran through a barbed wire fence and, at some point, threw Burks out. The grass truck was completely destroyed.

Travis Burks went by private car to Texoma Medical Center. Chief Burks said his son is bruised and cut and required several stitches, but is basically all right and was released after being treated in the emergency room.

Chief Burks said that people in the Bells fire district will still be able to expect good service from the Bells FD, in spite of losing one of its two grass trucks.

Bells Fire Chief Tommy Carter stepped forward and said that Bells FD has an out-of-commission engine which Savoy can use until its fleet is again fully equipped and that other departments might step up with help, as they did last year when Van Alstyne FD fire engine was damaged in a wreck. Savoy FD has a mutual aid agreement with Bells FD and also relies on fire departments from other nearby towns, such as Whitewright.

A strap holding the water tank on the flatbed came undone, causing the grass truck to shift its load and become off-balanced.

"Half the load went off the truck," said Chief Burks.

The grass truck was completely destroyed, said Halford.

Savoy's second grass truck and Bells firefighters answered the original grass fire call, said Carter.

[Photograph caption:] Dan Bouge
Herald Democrat

A man photographs what's left of a Savoy Fire Department grass truck Wednesday evening after it rolled one mile south of Savoy on FM 1752.
